purpose: Source-reconciled technical inventory of subscription, checkout, billing-event and provider-state surfaces relevant to the still-open BILLING_CANCELLATION_REFUND_POLICY decision. Field markers are restricted to names observed in the current database schema and expected migration corpus; this registry does not decide customer-facing policy or provider behavior.

canonical_open_decision.required: Approved trial, renewal, cancellation, refund/withdrawal, delinquency and reactivation policy.
canonical_open_decision.resolution_authority: business plus legal review after real billing authority

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The current model represents trial state and trial boundaries. Those fields do not define withdrawal rights, cancellation timing, conversion behavior or customer notice obligations.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: When and how may a customer cancel during trial?
What happens to access after trial cancellation?
What notice is required before trial conversion or expiration?
How does the policy behave while billing authority is unavailable?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Current billing-period and price markers exist technically. They do not establish post-cancellation service entitlement, refund amount, renewal disclosure or price-change policy.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Does paid access continue through current_period_end after cancellation?
Under what reviewed circumstances may access end earlier?
Do monthly and yearly plans have different cancellation or refund rules?
How are renewal and price changes disclosed?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The schema contains cancel_at_period_end but no dedicated canceled_at column in the current authoritative schema. The flag is therefore only a technical intent marker, not an approved customer cancellation rule or effective-date record.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: What customer action may set cancel_at_period_end?
What confirmation must be shown or sent?
Can a scheduled cancellation be reversed before the period ends?
Which independently reviewed event establishes effective cancellation?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The current model can represent subscription status and audited transitions but has no dedicated delinquent_since column in the authoritative schema. Status transitions do not establish grace duration, retry cadence, suspension timing, recovery rules or customer notice.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Which provider-confirmed event moves a subscription into delinquency?
Is there a grace period and, if so, what independently reviewed rule defines it?
What product access changes are allowed during delinquency?
What retry, recovery and communication rules apply?
When may delinquency lead to terminal cancellation?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Terminal subscription state can be reflected by status plus authority-event transitions. Those technical records do not define cancellation rights, refund eligibility, post-cancellation access, customer communication or data-retention treatment.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Which causes may produce terminal cancellation?
What real provider or owner evidence authorizes each cancellation path?
What customer confirmation and effective date are required?
What happens to account access and retained data after cancellation?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Checkout intents contain provider_checkout_ref and lifecycle metadata. A checkout-intent status does not establish that money moved, that a refund occurred or that a customer cancellation right was exercised.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: How are abandoned, expired, failed and canceled checkout attempts communicated?
How are duplicate or repeated payment attempts handled?
What provider evidence is required before treating a charge as paid?
How must failed, duplicated or disputed charges be escalated?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Webhook receipts provide authenticated-event and processing metadata using the current schema. They remain operational reconciliation records, not customer terms or proof of provider financial truth without the authorized billing evidence chain.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Which real provider events are authoritative for payment, cancellation, delinquency and refund transitions?
How are duplicate, late, unauthenticated or failed events handled?
What customer communication follows a material billing-state reconciliation?
Which receipts must be retained under the future approved retention matrix?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The current authority-event ledger captures plan/status transitions, source metadata, external references and digests. It is an audit surface, not the customer contract, refund decision or legal approval record.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Which cancellation, refund and delinquency decisions require an authority event?
Which authority_source values are allowed after real billing activation?
Which provider or human decisions require a separate receipt?
How long must this audit trail be retained?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: Plan, price and fee-assumption metadata can support calculations and versioning. Current fields use effective_until, variable_bps and fixed_amount_minor; none establishes refund amount, proration, tax treatment, fee pass-through or required customer disclosure.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Under which reviewed circumstances is a refund full, partial, prorated or unavailable?
How are taxes and real provider fees treated after provider evidence exists?
Which price and evidence version applies when a financial reversal is reviewed?
What disclosure is required for renewals and price changes?

technical_surfaces.technical_observation: The current schema separates provider registry lifecycle, selection state and private external-evidence fields. Asaas remains selected_pending_credentials and inactive; provider selection or registry capabilities do not prove real production refund/cancellation behavior.
policy_questions_for_future_real_review: Which provider-native cancellation and refund capabilities are actually available after real activation?
Which provider receipts are required for a real financial reversal?
What happens when reviewed customer policy requires an outcome that provider mechanics cannot complete automatically?
Which provider timing, fee or operational constraints require customer disclosure after real evidence review?

cross_surface_unresolved_policy_decision: delinquency trigger, grace, retry and suspension
refund or withdrawal eligibility and review window
full versus partial versus prorated refund
tax and real provider fee handling
provider cancellation and refund mechanics after real activation
data and access treatment after cancellation
resolution_authority: business plus legal review after real billing authority
